native_result.query: In which years were individuals with a criminal record found to have significantly lower wealth compared to those without?
native_result.HypoA: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
native_result.HypoB: In the NLS 1979 cohort, respondents who reported any jail stay between 1985 and 1994 had significantly lower composite wealth than those who did not at every measured wealth year — 1985, 1990, and 1996 — under both Welch's t-test (all p < 2e-19) and the Mann–Whitney U test (all p < 1e-9), surviving Bonferroni correction at α = 0.05/3. The deficit grew from −$17,157 in 1985 to −$57,598 in 1990 to −$85,063 in 1996 (Cohen's d = −0.17, −0.26, −0.32); rank-biserial peaked at 0.42 in 1990. The 1985 and 1990 associations are contemporaneous with the exposure window; only the 1996 result has the exposure preceding the wealth measurement.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (n=12,013, no missing values, 289 jailed / 11,724 not). Per-year cross-sectional comparisons of composite_wealth_<year> between ever_jailed=1 and ever_jailed=0 using Welch's two-sample t-test (unequal variances, unequal n) and the rank-based Mann–Whitney U test as a robustness check given the heavy right-skew of wealth (skew 6.5–16.8). Negative wealth values were retained. Both raw alpha=0.05 and Bonferroni alpha=0.05/3 thresholds applied. No covariates added. All three years rejected the null at both thresholds under both tests.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.

sub_hypo.text: In the NLS 1979 cohort, respondents jailed at any time between 1985 and 1994 had significantly lower composite wealth in 1985, 1990, and 1996 than respondents not jailed during that window, with an increasing absolute wealth deficit across measured years.
sub_hypo.context: NLS 1979 cohort: 12,013 respondents, comprising 289 jailed and 11,724 not jailed between 1985 and 1994, with no missing values. Per-year cross-sectional comparisons used no covariates and retained negative wealth values. Wealth in 1985 and 1990 was measured within the exposure window; only the 1996 wealth measurement followed the exposure window.
sub_hypo.relations: Jailed respondents had lower composite wealth in every measured year: jailed-minus-not-jailed deficits were −$17,157 in 1985, −$57,598 in 1990, and −$85,063 in 1996, with Cohen's d of −0.17, −0.26, and −0.32, respectively. Rank-biserial peaked at 0.42 in 1990. All comparisons were significant under unequal-variance Welch's two-sample t-test (all p < 2e-19) and the rank-based Mann–Whitney U robustness test (all p < 1e-9), at both raw α = 0.05 and Bonferroni α = 0.05/3. The Mann–Whitney U test addressed heavy right-skew in wealth (skew 6.5–16.8). Associations in 1985 and 1990 were contemporaneous with the exposure window; exposure preceded wealth measurement only in 1996.
